tasks.short: Prepare and distribute educational leaflets, pamphlets and visual aids

steps.what: Select educational information and suitable visual sources
Write leaflet and pamphlet explanations for the intended audience

loop.purpose: Draft plain explanations from selected educational sources
loop.input: Selected sources, intended audience and requested message
loop.output: Editable educational draft with source references
loop.check: Educator verifies agricultural or home-management meaning, safe instructions and reading level against the sources
loop.stop: One correction pass then manual writing for unsupported instructions
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates do not express the topic-specific explanation at the required reading level

steps.what: Lay out leaflets, pamphlets and visual aids
Check the educational proof and select its final distribution version
Print the final leaflets and pamphlets
Distribute the final educational materials to participants

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates for layout and bounded drafting to explain selected source material. The educator checks the final proof, prints it and distributes that version as separate actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated explanation writing and manual layout consume preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates handle page structure while a checked drafting loop assists the prose.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong food-safety or agricultural instructions can harm readers.
tasks.human_edge: The educator chooses reliable advice and checks that the audience can use it safely.
tasks.altitude: More preparation time can go to source quality and practical illustrations.

reach.task: Make practical information understandable to different audiences

evidence.claim: LessonUp can rewrite lesson slide text by tone or level; this supports assisted educational wording, not verified agricultural recommendations or the time estimate.
Native page templates and checked topic drafting are a model-knowledge design for leaflets.

assumptions: Boundary includes source selection, writing, layout, final proof, printing and physical distribution. Printing and distribution retain their actual effort.

The educator captures audience, message, selected source and image choices in s1 and s2; their time is counted. Layout uses s2 text plus the existing native template. Missing content returns to manual composition, never invented advice.

The educator selects the master and intended audience in s4, and checks print quantity in s5. Changes to the master invalidate print and distribution permission; physical copies are checked against that master before handout.
Test native templates and plain-language aids before custom code. Savings concern real prose and layout work, not internal file saves.
unknowns: Actual split between printed and digital materials
research_questions: Does corrected plain-language drafting preserve every condition in the source advice?

already_counted.description: Draft correction, final proof and print/distribution checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain templates and review source freshness and drafting errors.

approvals.approved_version: Exact educational master version checked in s4 and print quantity checked in s5; changed content requires a new proof check.
Printed copies matching the checked master and intended participant audience checked before s6 distribution; changes void the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R68, gross32 minus6 upkeep gives net26. Range8-18 assumes repeated leaflet formats and checked prose assistance, with printing and distribution unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule and make regular farmer visits

steps.what: Look up farmers' contact details and previous visit dates
Agree visit purpose and availability with farmers
Record the agreed visit time, location and purpose
Send the farmer the final visit confirmation
Travel to the farm for the scheduled visit
Make the farmer visit and discuss current needs
Record the completed visit and follow-up needs

tasks.design: Link the native {CRM} contact view to contextual {CALENDAR} appointment entry and a short completed-visit form. The educator agrees arrangements, sends the checked confirmation, travels and makes the visit; no travel or relationship time is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact lookup and repeated appointment details interrupt scheduling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and contextual forms can retain farmer and visit identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Availability changes with farm work and a visit can reveal unexpected needs.
tasks.human_edge: The educator builds trust and interprets the farm context.
tasks.altitude: Small scheduling and record-entry gains; visits remain personal.

reach.task: Connect farm observations to practical teaching needs

evidence.claim: Linked contact views and contextual appointment forms can reduce repeated scheduling entry; this farmer-visit estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes scheduling, actual confirmation, travel, farmer visit and the completed-visit record, in lifecycle order.

The existing contact record supplies farmer id, contact channel and address. The educator checks them in s1, obtains date, time and purpose in s2, and captures those fields in s3. A structured address is not assumed from an unrecorded conversation.
Visit outcome and follow-up text are produced by the educator in s7, with capture time retained. Missing address or availability requires manual clarification within the scheduling steps.
Test native contact-to-appointment entry and contextual visit forms before custom code. No automatic send, route optimizer or extra reminder is implied; internal saves earn no saving.
unknowns: Whether contact data are already linked to appointments
Time spent on appointment entry versus travel
research_questions: Does contextual entry save time after contact checking and missing-address clarification are included?

already_counted.description: Agreement, appointment capture, confirmation checking and visit-record writing remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain linked views and remove stale form defaults.

approvals.approved_version: Exact farmer recipient, appointment time, address and purpose checked in the final confirmation before s4; any change requires recheck.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R94, gross6 minus2 upkeep gives net4. Range0-2 assumes repeated identifiers are currently entered manually; travel and visiting retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Organize, advise and participate in community activities and organizations

steps.what: Discuss community activity needs and agree responsibilities
Write the community activity plan and responsibility list
Send final community activity arrangements to participating organisers
Organize the activity on site and coordinate practical changes
Advise participants and participate in the community activity

tasks.design: Use a reusable {DOCS} activity-plan template for the written arrangements, with current responsibilities entered by the educator. Discussion, the final arrangements message, on-site coordination and community participation remain separate human steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing recurring activity plans repeats headings and standard practical instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document reuse can retain the stable structure without deciding this event's arrangements.
tasks.still_hard: Community priorities and practical conditions change during the event.
tasks.human_edge: The educator reconciles local expectations and gives relevant advice.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive plan structure; community responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Inclusive participation and practical event planning

evidence.claim: Reusable native activity plans can reduce repeated formatting and standard text while leaving event decisions and participation human; savings are model knowledge.

assumptions: The US examples are treated as local community learning events in the European setting. Boundary includes the actual written plan and external communication, not just participation.
The educator obtains date, venue, activities, responsible people and constraints through s1 and records them in s2. All capture time is retained; the template supplies structure only.
No structured participation flag, permission status or attendance list is inferred. Missing arrangements return to manual discussion and plan writing.
Test native reusable documents first; no model is needed. Only repeated structure and standard text lose time. Internal saves have no saving or self-approval.
unknowns: Whether recurring plans already use templates
How much organisation involves genuinely repeated text
research_questions: How much plan-writing time remains after current details and responsibilities are entered?

already_counted.description: Current plan capture, decisions and final arrangements-message checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Keep the standard activity-plan sections current.

approvals.approved_version: Exact activity-plan version, responsibilities, dates and external organiser recipients checked before sending s3; changes void the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R95, gross5 minus1 upkeep gives net4. Range0-2 assumes recurring written plans with some repeated structure; community discussion and participation retain full time.

tasks.short: Conduct agricultural research, analyze data and prepare research reports

steps.what: Design the agricultural research and analysis protocol
Conduct agricultural field research and take measurements
Record and check research measurements and observation metadata
Calculate research summaries and prepare analysis tables
Analyze agricultural results and record conclusions and limitations
Write the agricultural research report

loop.purpose: Draft the report from protocol, tables and researcher conclusions
loop.input: Protocol, verified tables and interpretation notes
loop.output: Report draft with table and source references
loop.check: Educator checks causal language, limitations, methods and every reported result against the dataset and intended interpretation
loop.stop: One correction pass then manual reporting if claims are unsupported
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can arrange sections but cannot express the researcher's particular interpretation

steps.what: Check and finish the research report

tasks.design: Configure repeatable calculations in {SPREADSHEET} against the checked dataset and protocol. A bounded drafting loop in {DOCS} uses the resulting tables and the educator's interpretation; fieldwork, data capture, research judgement and final report checking remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated table construction and report prose consume time after measurements are available.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calculation templates and source-bound drafting can support repeatable analysis and reporting.
tasks.still_hard: Research validity depends on sampling, confounding and field conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The educator distinguishes a useful local observation from an unsupported general recommendation.
tasks.altitude: More analysis time can go to validity checks rather than repeated tables and prose.

reach.task: Explain the limits of field research findings
reach.learn: Study design and reproducible agricultural analysis

evidence.claim: Native calculation templates and checked model drafting can support research tables and reports; this agricultural design and estimate are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes the research protocol, fieldwork, data capture, calculations, interpretation and finished report. No publication or external submission is proposed.

The educator produces plot or sample id, observation time, treatment, measurement, unit and missing-data reason in s2 and s3; capture and checking time remains full. The protocol in s1 names the planned calculations and exclusion rules.

Native formulas in s4 produce tables only after s3 checking. Missing units, ambiguous identifiers or incompatible study designs stop the calculation and return to manual analysis; no free discrepancy code or validated dataset is assumed.

The educator writes conclusions and limitations in s5 with full time retained. Test native formulas, pivots and report templates before custom code or drafting loops. Existing automated calculations and same-system saves earn no new saving.
research_questions: Can a repeat calculation reproduce the manually verified results without new data-cleaning work?
Does report drafting preserve the educator's limits on causal claims?

already_counted.description: Dataset capture, interpretation notes, report correction and final checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain calculation templates, regression checks and drafting sources.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R79, gross21 minus5 upkeep gives net16. Range3-10 assumes repeatable studies with current manual table construction and report prose; all fieldwork and interpretation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Field visits, education and research judgement stay human while selected record, layout and reporting work becomes shorter.
reach: Exchange field-research methods with agricultural sciences teachers
Coordinate practical public learning with self-enrichment teachers
skills_to_grow: Check practical educational advice against sources
role.ambitious_version: An educator who spends less time repeating document and record structures and more time interpreting local needs and evidence.
